Interventions are one of the most critical parts of HPVsim. This tutorial shows how to implement standard interventions, as well as how to define your own custom interventions.

Click [here](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/starsimhub/hpvsim/HEAD?urlpath=lab%2Ftree%2Fdocs%2Ftutorials%2Ftut_interventions.ipynb) to open an interactive version of this notebook.

</div>

## Products and interventions

HPVsim contains *products*, which can be thought of as the actual test, diagnostic, treatment, or vaccine product being used, as well as *interventions*, which deliver those products to the people in the simulation.
Information about the default products included with HPVsim (e.g. attributes like test positivity and efficacy) are available in the `hpvsim/data/products_*.csv` files. Specifically:

* Screening products (VIA, Pap smears, liquid-based cytology, HPV testing, and HPV16/18 testing): `hpvsim/data/products_dx.csv`
* Treatment products (ablation, excision, and therapeutic vaccines): `hpvsim/data/products_tx.csv`
* Prophylactic vaccine products (bivalent, quadrivalent, nonavalent): `hpvsim/data/products_vx.csv`

It's also possible to make a custom product, e.g.

```{python}
import hpvsim as hpv
import pandas as pd
my_treatment_data = pd.DataFrame({'name':'new_tx', 'state':['precin','cin1','cin2','cin3','cancerous'],'genotype':'all','efficacy':[.2,.3,.3,.4,.4]})
my_treatment = hpv.tx(df=my_treatment_data)
```

Custom products can be made for diagnostics and vaccination in the same way. The efficacy of some products varies by genotype, in which case efficacy values for each genotype can be entered as separate dataframe rows.

Most of the time, it isn't necessary to create your own products if you just want to use one of the standard options. When setting up screening, triage, or treatment interventions, it's possible to pass in a string that will create a standard default product.

## Screening and treatment interventions

Screening and treatment is implemented in HPVsim as a flexible set of interventions that can be mixed and matched. By specifying how each of the components link together, it's possible to create quite complex algorithms. This is illustrated in the following example:

```{python}
import starsim as ss

# Define a series of interventions to screen, triage, assign treatment, and administer treatment
prob = 0.6
screen      = hpv.routine_screening(start_year=2015, prob=prob, product='via', name='screen') # Routine screening
to_triage   = lambda sim: sim.interventions['screen'].outcomes['positive'] # Define who's eligible for triage
triage      = hpv.routine_triage(eligibility=to_triage, prob=prob, product='hpv', name='triage') # Triage people
to_treat    = lambda sim: sim.interventions['triage'].outcomes['positive'] # Define who's eligible to be assigned treatment
assign_tx   = hpv.routine_triage(eligibility=to_treat, prob=prob, product='tx_assigner', name='assign_tx') # Assign treatment
to_ablate   = lambda sim: sim.interventions['assign_tx'].outcomes['ablation'] # Define who's eligible for ablation treatment
ablation    = hpv.treat_num(eligibility=to_ablate, prob=prob, product='ablation') # Administer ablation
to_excise   = lambda sim: sim.interventions['assign_tx'].outcomes['excision'] # Define who's eligible for excision
excision    = hpv.treat_delay(delay=1.0, eligibility=to_excise, prob=prob, product='excision') # Administer excision

# Define the parameters
pars = dict(
    n_agents      = 20e3,       # Population size
    start         = 2000,       # Simulation start year
    stop          = 2035,       # Simulation end year
    verbose       = 0,          # Don't print details of the run
    rand_seed     = 2,          # Set a non-default seed
    genotypes     = [16, 18],   # Include the two genotypes of greatest general interest
)

# Create the sim with and without interventions
orig_sim = hpv.Sim(**pars, label='Baseline')
sim = hpv.Sim(**pars, interventions=[screen, triage, assign_tx, ablation, excision], label='With screen & treat')

# Run and plot
msim = ss.MultiSim([orig_sim, sim]).run(parallel=False)
msim.plot();
```

A few things to note here:

* Each intervention is given a unique `name`. Downstream interventions reference an upstream one's results through `sim.interventions['<name>'].outcomes[...]`, which is how the cascade is wired together. A treatment intervention's `name` must differ from its `product` (they share a namespace), so the leaf treatments above are left unnamed.
* Interventions are passed to the sim via the `interventions=` argument.
* Several of the interventions above are defined as routine interventions, e.g. `hpv.routine_screening()` and `hpv.routine_triage()`. In general, most interventions exist as both routine and campaign versions. The difference between the two comes down to how the dates are interpreted:
    * `hpv.routine_screening(start_year=2020, end_year=2030, prob=0.2)` implies that the intervention will be in place each year between 2020-2030;
    * `hpv.campaign_screening(years=[2020, 2030], prob=0.2)` implies that the intervention will be delivered twice: once in 2020 and once in 2030.

The script `examples/t05_screen_algorithms.py` shows how to set up each of the seven algorithms recommended in the WHO's guidelines for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions (see https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK572308/).

## Prophylactic vaccination

Prophylactic vaccination protects people before they are exposed to HPV by offering a vaccine to a chosen group — typically to girls within a target age range, before sexual debut.

```{python}
vx = hpv.routine_vx(prob=prob, start_year=2015, age_range=[9,10], product='bivalent', name='vaccination')

# Create the sim with and without interventions
orig_sim = hpv.Sim(**pars, label='Baseline')
sim = hpv.Sim(**pars, interventions=vx, label='With vaccination')

# Run and plot
msim = ss.MultiSim([orig_sim, sim]).run(parallel=False)
msim.plot();
```

<div class="alert alert-success">

Note that probabilities passed to interventions are annual probabilities, not total.

</div>

## Therapeutic vaccination

Therapeutic vaccination can be delivered in a couple of ways:

* as a mass campaign that reaches women in a target age range regardless of whether they have been screened, and
* as part of a screen-and-treat pathway that reaches the women who screen positive.

The following example illustrates both. Mass therapeutic vaccination delivers a product to women within a given age range directly (here a campaign dose plus an ongoing routine dose); screen-linked therapeutic vaccination uses `hpv.linked_txvx`, which offers the vaccine to the women who screened positive in an upstream screening intervention.

```{python}
# Mass therapeutic vaccination: a one-off campaign dose plus an ongoing routine dose
campaign_txvx = hpv.campaign_txvx(prob=0.9, years=2015, age_range=[30, 50], product='txvx1', name='campaign txvx')
routine_txvx  = hpv.routine_txvx(prob=0.8, start_year=2016, age_range=[30, 31], product='txvx2', name='routine txvx')
mass_vx_intvs = [campaign_txvx, routine_txvx]

# Therapeutic vaccination delivered through screening: screen, then vaccinate the positives
screened_pos   = lambda sim: sim.interventions['routine screening'].outcomes['positive']
routine_screen = hpv.routine_screening(start_year=2016, product='hpv', prob=0.1, age_range=[30, 50], name='routine screening')
deliver_txvx   = hpv.linked_txvx(prob=0.8, product='txvx1', eligibility=screened_pos, name='txvx')
screen_vx_intv = [routine_screen, deliver_txvx]

sim0 = hpv.Sim(**pars, label='Baseline')
sim1 = hpv.Sim(**pars, interventions=mass_vx_intvs, label='Mass therapeutic vaccination')
sim2 = hpv.Sim(**pars, interventions=screen_vx_intv, label='Therapeutic vaccination through screening')

# Run and plot
msim = ss.MultiSim([sim0, sim1, sim2]).run(parallel=False)
msim.plot();
```
